subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group: cross-agent sessions_list visibility mismatch causes one-way sessions_send failure

question: Should same-Telegram-group cross-agent sessions become mutually visible/sendable under the current visibility model, or should this wait for an explicit per-capability/per-agent authorization contract?
rationale: The apparent fix changes a cross-agent session security boundary, and the existing docs intentionally couple send/list/history/status visibility behind one dial plus A2A policy.

options.title: Approve a bounded contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the send/list/history/status split, then implement the Telegram A/B case against that approved contract.

options.title: Allow send-only A2A now
options.body: Permit sessions_send to rely on A2A policy while keeping list/history/status visibility-gated, with live Telegram proof and regression coverage.

options.title: Document current behavior as expected
options.body: Keep requiring visibility=all plus A2A for cross-agent group access and document that shared group membership is not an implicit trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers decide the send/list/history/status split, then implement the Telegram A/B case against that approved contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is prior ownership of the sandbox visibility and session access helper boundary that would need to change.
